input.content: Pattern: "Simplification" that drops an ownership/identity guard before a state mutation causes eviction of UNRELATED state. Example: cleanup_setup(store, workspace_id, setup_id) originally removed the workspace's active association only when active[workspace_id]["setup_id"] == setup_id. A refactor replaced the guarded removal with an unconditional store.active.pop(workspace_id, None). Regression: cleaning up a stale/superseded/cancelled setup for a workspace silently evicts the CURRENTLY active setup's association (active_connection returns None). Reachable via public API because complete_setup overwrites active[workspace_id] and begin_setup allows multiple pending setups per workspace. Existing test stayed green because it only covered the matching-setup case. Review heuristic: when a diff deletes a conditional immediately before a pop/delete/overwrite, ask "did that condition scope the mutation to the correct owner?" — a passing same-key test does not cover the cross-key/superseded case. Severity P1 (correctness + silent state loss).
